operations.tipReorderDesc: Rules run from top to bottom.
operations.emptyHelpLink: New here? Read the guide and regex basics

about.title: About Project
about.description: A simple, powerful, and open-source cross-platform batch renaming tool that supports Windows, macOS, and Linux.
about.bio: Hi! I'm Junyou. This project was created to make tedious file renaming tasks easier. If you find this tool helpful, consider buying me a coffee to support continued development and maintenance!
about.thanks: Thank you for your support and encouragement
about.changelogError: Couldn't reach GitHub to load the changelog. Check your connection, or try again in a few minutes.
about.changelogEmpty: No changelog entries are available yet
about.postUpdateTitle: Updated successfully to v{version}. Here's what's new.
about.updateInstallStarted: Update installation started. Restart the app after the installer finishes.
about.updateInstallFailedFallback: Update install failed. Opening the download page instead.
about.updateInstallBlockedMac: This app location is not suitable for direct in-app updates. Opening the download page instead.

basic.title: Basic Workflow
basic.step1: Drag & drop files into the file area or click to select files.
basic.step2: Add rules in the "Rename Pipeline" section.
basic.step4: Preview renamed results in real-time on the right table.
basic.step5: Click "Rename Files" or "Create Copy" once confirmed.

pipeline.title: Rule Order & Pipeline Chaining
pipeline.description: Rules are executed sequentially from top to bottom:
pipeline.point1: The output filename of each rule automatically becomes the input for the next rule.
pipeline.point2: Different rule ordering produces different results. Reorder anytime via drag handles or arrow buttons.
pipeline.tip: Tip: You can temporarily disable any rule by clicking the eye icon without deleting it.

regex.title: Regex Cheat Sheet
regex.description: Regular Expressions (Regex) are powerful text matching tools that help you precisely select the parts of text you want to modify.

table.word: Matches any letter, digit, or underscore
table.star: Matches 0 or more of the preceding character
table.plus: Matches 1 or more of the preceding character
table.caret: Matches the start of the string
table.dollar: Matches the end of the string

numbering.title: Sequential Numbering (${'{'}n{'}'})
numbering.description: You can use {code} in the "Replace with" field to insert incrementing numbers.

ai.title: AI assistant
ai.description: No regex needed: describe how you want files renamed in plain words and the AI writes the rules. It can also explain what your current rules do.
ai.cliTitle: Option 1: an AI CLI you already use
ai.cliDesc: If you're signed in to Claude Code, Codex or Grok CLI, just pick it. No API key needed, and it uses the CLI's current model.
ai.apiDesc: Add a Gemini, OpenAI or Anthropic key in Settings › AI Assistant, or connect a local Ollama. Keys stay on this computer.
ai.example2: Remove “final”, “copy” and “(1)” from the names and replace spaces with underscores
ai.example3: Explain what the current rules do
ai.examplesTip: Tip: a single “before → after” example is the clearest way to explain what you want.
ai.privacy: Each request sends your message, the current rules and up to 30 filenames — never file contents.

ai.title: AI Rule Assistant
ai.autoApplyDesc: Automatically update the rule pipeline and live preview when AI generates new rules
ai.onboardingDesc: This feature interacts directly with your local Claude Code CLI using your subscription without API keys. Run the following commands in your terminal:

ai.onboardingGrokDesc: This feature interacts directly with your local xAI Grok CLI without needing API keys. Run the following commands in your terminal:
ai.stepLoginCli: Log in to your Claude account
ai.stepLoginCodexCli: Log in to your OpenAI account
ai.stepLoginGrokCli: Log in to your xAI account
ai.welcomeSubtitle: Describe your renaming needs in natural language, or let AI analyze current filenames to construct a regex pipeline.
ai.quickPromptAnalyze: Analyze current file patterns and generate clean standardized rules
ai.quickPromptExtractDate: Extract dates in filenames and move them to the front with hyphens
ai.quickPromptRemoveSpaces: Remove redundant spaces/special characters, and convert underscores to hyphens
ai.quickPromptAddSequence: Keep main filename and append a 2-digit sequence number at the end
ai.thinking: Claude is analyzing files and thinking...
ai.codexThinking: Codex is analyzing files and thinking...
ai.grokThinking: Grok is analyzing files and thinking...
ai.inputPlaceholder: Describe your renaming request (e.g., move the prefix date to the end)...
ai.enterToSend: Press Enter to send, Shift + Enter for new line
ai.onboardingGeminiDesc: This feature connects directly to Google Gemini API. Click the button below to go to Settings > AI Assistant and enter your Google AI Studio API Key.
ai.geminiThinking: Gemini is analyzing files and thinking...
ai.onboardingApiKeyDesc: This feature connects directly to {name} API. Click the button below to go to Settings > AI Assistant and enter your API Key.
ai.rejectedSteps: Skipped {n} step(s) the app can't run (unknown type, missing plugin or invalid regex)
ai.quickPromptExplain: Explain what the current rules do
ai.quickPromptInfer: Infer the rules from my example, e.g. IMG_0001.jpg → 2026-01-01_001.jpg
ai.privacyTitle: What is sent to the AI
ai.privacyBody: Each request sends your message, recent chat, the current rules, and up to 30 filenames from the list with their preview. File contents are never sent. With an API profile the data goes to the provider you chose; with a CLI profile it is handled by that CLI.
